pages.title: About
pages.content:
ABOUT THE SCHOOL

About

Hibari Flight School was founded in 2011 by Margit Halvorsen and Ruth Abernathy at Brackmoor Airfield in Alder Vale. Setting up operations in Hangar 2 with two light training aircraft, Margit served as head of training while Ruth oversaw maintenance as chief engineer. Their goal from the outset was to create a calm, disciplined flight school rooted in genuine airmanship and regional grass-roots flying, away from the rushed environment of commercial flight academies.

Over the following years, the school steadily grew while maintaining its focused, personal atmosphere on the airfield. Hangar 2 expanded its fleet to include three two-seat low-wing trainers dedicated to ab-initio instruction and one four-seat touring aircraft for cross-country navigation exercises. Additional instructors joined the roster to lead ground-school courses, night ratings, and advanced navigation, all sharing the core conviction that every safe pilot first learns to understand the local weather and grass runway conditions.

Today, Hibari Flight School continues to operate from Brackmoor Airfield along runway 09/27, using both the 780-metre grass strip and the 640-metre asphalt surface. Students train six days a week from early morning until sunset, flying dual lessons, conducting thorough pre-flight walk-rounds, and mastering cross-country journeys across the Vale. More than a decade after its first flight, the school remains committed to patient, one-to-one flight instruction where reading the wind comes first.

pages.title: Licences
pages.content:
WHICH LICENCES WE TEACH

Licences

The Private Pilot Licence (PPL) is the full international private pilot qualification: 45 hours minimum, usually 9–14 months, budget from $13,500. Most students fly 50–60 hours before the test; this is an estimate, not a promise.

The Light Aircraft Pilot Licence (LAPL) is a focused licence for recreational flying in regional airspace: 30 hours minimum, usually 6–10 months, budget from $9,200.

The Night Rating adds privileges to fly after dark: 5 hours after the PPL, budget from $1,350. Not sure yet? Start with a 40-minute trial flight, $190.

pages.title: Lesson block
pages.content:
HOW A LESSON BLOCK IS FLOWN

Lesson block

One block is two hours on the field. Seventy minutes of it are in the air or on the way to it.

Brief (25 min): review the weather, examine the airfield circuit and set clear goals for the sortie. Walk-round (20 min): inspect the airframe, fuel samples, control hinges and propeller together. Fly (60 min): climb out from runway 09/27 for handling, circuit practice or navigation across the Vale. Debrief (15 min): shut down on the apron, review your circuits in the logbook and prepare the focus for your next lesson.

If the weather is below minima we cancel by 07:00 at no charge and rebook the block.

pages.title: Trial flight
pages.content:
COME AND READ THE WIND WITH US

Trial flight

A trial flight is 40 minutes airborne with a briefing, aircraft, fuel, instructor and Brackmoor landing fees included: $190. You can fly from age 14, up to 110 kg.

Choose a morning online or by phone, receive confirmation within one working day, arrive at Hangar 2 thirty minutes early with photo ID, then brief with your instructor and take the controls for 40 minutes. Weather cancellations are made by 07:00 and rebooked free.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
WHAT FLYING COSTS

Fees

All prices in USD and include aircraft, fuel, instructor and landing fees at Brackmoor. The examiner’s fee for the licence test is paid to the examiner.

  • Trial flight, 40 minutes airborne, with briefing: $190
  • Dual lesson, per flight hour: $245
  • Solo hire, per flight hour: $195
  • Lesson block bundle, 10 flight hours prepaid: $2,350
  • Ground school, PPL theory course (10 evenings): $680
  • Night rating course (5 flight hours): $1,350
  • Licence test aircraft hire (up to 2 hours): $440

Most students fly 50–60 hours before the test; budget from $13,500.

pages.title: Crew
pages.content:
THE PEOPLE AT HANGAR 2

Crew

Margit Halvorsen, Head of training. Co-founded Hibari Flight School in 2011 and oversees all flight instruction and syllabus standards at Brackmoor Airfield.

Ruth Abernathy, Chief engineer. Co-founded the school in 2011 and manages aircraft airworthiness, maintenance, and fleet inspections in Hangar 2.

Tomás Ferreira, Flight instructor. Instructing at Brackmoor since 2014, specializing in foundation flying skills and traffic pattern discipline.

Aisha Rahman, Instructor, ground-school lead. Joined the school in 2016 to lead PPL theory courses alongside regular dual flight training.

Kwame Mensah, Instructor, night rating. Teaching at Hibari since 2018 with a focus on night qualifications and instrument flying skills.

Ines Laurent, Operations & bookings. Overseeing airfield operations, student lesson schedules, and front desk enquiries since 2019.

Jonah Petrakis, Instructor, tailwheel & cross-country. Guiding students through cross-country navigation exercises and advanced handling since 2021.

pages.title: The Field
pages.content:
BRACKMOOR AIRFIELD

The Field

Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. Runway 09/27: grass 780 m and asphalt 640 m. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00 to sunset.

Hangar 2 houses three two-seat low-wing trainers and one four-seat touring aircraft used for cross-country flights.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
FIND US

Contact

Hibari Flight School, Hangar 2, Brackmoor Airfield, Field Road, Alder Vale. Phone +1 555 0142 0911, e-mail hello@hibariflight.example.

Flying Tuesday–Sunday, 08:00 to sunset. Office Tuesday–Saturday, 09:00–17:00. Closed Mondays.

posts.title: A first trial flight on a still Saturday
posts.excerpt: Martin Okonjo visited Brackmoor for an introductory flight and took the controls above Alder Vale in clear, gentle morning air.
posts.content:
Martin Okonjo arrived at Hangar 2 thirty minutes early with his photo ID, as the confirmation said. The briefing took ten minutes, the walk-round another ten, and by half past eight he was strapped into the left seat.

Over the Vale the air was clear and still. He took the controls for most of the 40 minutes and landed on runway 09 with his instructor’s hands hovering, unused, near the stick.

posts.title: Priya’s first solo
posts.excerpt: After 18 hours of dual instruction and circuit practice, Priya Nair completed three solo circuits and landings on runway 09.
posts.content:
After 18 hours of dual instruction and circuit practice, Priya Nair completed three solo circuits and landings on runway 09. Her instructor stepped out at the hold, shut the door and walked back to the apron.

The first thing she said on the radio was the circuit call. The second was a laugh.

posts.title: Elena’s first cross-country
posts.excerpt: Elena Duarte navigated the cross-country route from Brackmoor to Calder Field and back, logging 74 nautical miles.
posts.content:
Elena Duarte navigated the cross-country route from Brackmoor to Calder Field and back, logging 74 nautical miles.

She planned it on the ground the evening before, checked the wind at the windsock in the morning and flew it with a map bag on her knee.

posts.title: Reading the windsock
posts.excerpt: A windsock tells you direction and strength at a glance. Here is what we look for before every sortie.
posts.content:
A windsock tells you the wind direction by where it points away from, and the strength by how far it stands out. Fully extended means roughly fifteen knots or more.

Before every sortie we walk out to it, look for a minute, and write down what we saw.

posts.title: Winter flying at Brackmoor
posts.excerpt: Short days, cold engines and clear air: what changes for students between November and February.
posts.content:
Winter days are short, so lesson blocks start earlier and the walk-round takes a little longer with frost on the wings.

The air is often the best of the year: dense, smooth and clear to the far end of the Vale.

posts.title: What ground school covers
posts.excerpt: Ten evenings, Tuesday and Thursday 19:00–21:00: the theory subjects behind the PPL examination.
posts.content:
The PPL theory course runs over ten evenings, Tuesday and Thursday 19:00–21:00, and costs $680.

It covers air law, navigation, meteorology, human performance, principles of flight and aircraft general knowledge.
